channel.title: Updated · Science
channel.description: Physics, space, chemistry, materials and Earth science

item.title: The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity
item.description: Models of slow mantle flow suggest continents rose for hundreds of millions of years and then sank, which would erase and then bury the rock record behind the Great Unconformity. (Santosh Dhungana, Nicolas Flament)

item.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
item.description: A physics-based model of Webb's camera, tuned with the gradient descent used to train neural networks, cuts noise in exoplanet images and revealed a planet that had gone unseen at one wavelength. (Rodrigo Ferrer-Chavez, Jason J. Wang, Katherine L. Bouman et al.)

item.title: NASA's Swift gamma-ray observatory ends its 22-year mission with a fiery re-entry
item.description: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, which tracked more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts, was predicted to fall out of orbit on 4 November after a failed rescue attempt, and NASA now lists it as having re-entered. (The Guardian, NASA)

item.title: A hidden companion star may be stirring Betelgeuse's atmosphere
item.description: Radio observations from the VLA and ALMA suggest a close companion star, Siwarha, distorts the atmosphere of the red supergiant Betelgeuse, which has otherwise recovered from its Great Dimming. (ScienceDaily (ALMA release), The Astronomical Journal)

item.title: Uranium cubes show Germany's last wartime reactor was far short of what it needed
item.description: A PNAS Nexus analysis of surviving uranium cubes and archives finds the B8 reactor would have needed 1,292 to 1,775 cubes, far more than the 664 used, contradicting Heisenberg's claim that it was nearly critical. (Ars Technica, PNAS Nexus)

item.title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
item.description: Cryogenic atom probe tomography with deuterium tracers gives the first direct observation of hydrogen dissolved in the gaps between metal atoms, and shows the metal's makeup decides where it sits. (Chao Huang, Saiyu Liu, Wenting Lv et al. · University of Sydney)

item.title: Enigmatic HCl detections as a potential signature of igneous activity on Mars
item.description: Seasonal hydrogen chloride spikes above fresh fissures on Mars's Alba Mons suggest gas seeping from hot magma, a possible sign that Mars is dormant rather than dead. (Alexander Trokhimovskiy, Daniel Mège, Oleg Korablev et al. · Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences)

item.title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
item.description: Evidence of chirality in manganese telluride supports altermagnetism as a real third class of magnetism that sits between ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. (Daniel Jost, Resham Babu Regmi, Eder G. Lomeli et al. · SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory)

item.title: Chemical traces of blood found in a 115-million-year-old dinosaur bone
item.description: A team led by Curtin University reports red blood cell-like structures and heme molecules inside the leg bone of a 115-million-year-old Brazilian dinosaur, the first chemical evidence of blood in a dinosaur. (Phys.org, The Conversation, Popular Science)

item.title: LHCb sees first evidence of the rarest beauty-particle decay yet observed
item.description: The upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN reports 3.2-sigma evidence for a beauty-particle decay into two muons that occurs about once per ten billion decays, consistent with the Standard Model. (BBC, University of Cambridge, Phys.org)

item.title: Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial
item.description: In a 90-patient phase 2 trial, ivonescimab plus chemotherapy before and after surgery gave a 70.1% major pathological response in resectable lung cancer. (Xiaoliang Zhao, Bin Zhang, Chenguang Li et al. · Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital, The Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University)

item.title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations
item.description: AutoDNA, an AI-run laboratory, coordinates over 20 instruments across more than 11,000 steps to carry out DNA synthesis, amplification and sequencing with minimal human intervention. (Mingyu Wu, Zhaoguo Wang, Jiabin Wang et al.)

item.title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer
item.description: Copper complexes of heteroaryl sulfones split apart when hit by visible light, releasing carbon radicals that enable fluoroalkylation of arenes and alkynes. (Zhiqiang Wei, Xiang Li, Lin Xiao et al. · Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, ShanghaiTech University)
